newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CHISOX VENTURA CELEBRATES RETURN WITH GAME-WINNER.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CHISOX VENTURA CELEBRATES RETURN WITH GAME-WINNER.

text.p: Robin Ventura celebrated his long-awaited season debut Thursday with an RBI-double in the eighth inning that lifted the Chicago White Sox to a 2-1 win over the Texas Rangers.

Ventura, who missed the first four months of the season after fracturing his right leg and dislocating his right ankle in spring training, grounded out in his first three at-bats before coming through in the eighth.
"I'll never forget this game, I was just happy to be out there again," said the slugging third baseman.

Dave Martinez began the eighth with a walk against starter Ken Hill (5-8) and moved to second on Ozzie Guillen's sacrifice. After Ray Durham popped out, Ventura lined the first pitch into left-centre, scoring Martinez for a 2-1 lead.

Ventura was 1-for-12 lifetime against Hill before the double. The clutch hit made a winner of Matt Karchner (3-0), who relieved starter Doug Drabek and gave up a leadoff homer to Dean Palmer in the top of the eighth that tied it 1-1.
Roberto Hernandez worked the ninth for his 26th save.
The win moved Chicago within 3 1/2 games of first-place Cleveland in the American League Central.
White Sox manager Terry Bevington said: "It kind of choked you up a little to see Robin get that game-winning hit. I'm very proud of him and so is this team."
Texas lost for the seventh time in eight games.

In Cleveland, Randy Johnson struck out 11 over seven innings and became the second 14-game winner in the American League as the Seattle Mariners dealt the Cleveland Indians their worst loss ever at Jacobs Field, 11-1.
The 10-run trouncing eclipsed the Indians' 14-6 defeat to the Rangers in 1994, their first year at Jacobs Field.

Johnson (14-2), trailing only Toronto's Roger Clemens, who has 16 wins, allowed one run and seven hits with a walk. The lanky lefthander has recorded 10 or more strikeouts 11 times this year. He has lost just twice in his last 37 starts, dating back to August 1, 1995.

"They are a good-hitting team," said Johnson. "And they are probably the closest thing, if not the equivalent, to our offence in every aspect. They had opportunities to have big innings, but I just made pitches when I had to."
Johnson improved his major-league leading strikeout total to 209, his sixth season with at least 200 strikeouts.
"I remember in 1978 with the Yankees, Ron Guidry went 25-3," said Seattle manager Lou Piniella.

"Randy has gone well beyond that, and he's done it for a number of years now. I've said it before, and I don't want to slight anyone, because there are a lot of great pitchers, but he's at the top of his class."
Jay Buhner had three hits, two RBI and three runs scored, while Dan Wilson and Russ Davis had three RBI each.

In Toronto, Carlos Delgado hit his third grand slam of the season and Woody Williams pitched six innings for his third straight win as the Toronto Blue Jays edged the Milwaukee Brewers 5-4 for a sweep of their three-game set.

Delgado, batting clean-up, stepped to the plate with the bases loaded in the first inning and put Brewers starter Jose Mercedes (3-6) into a sudden 4-0 hole by hammering his 22nd homer of the season over the right-centre field fence.
Williams improved to 6-8 as Kelvim Escobar notched his fourth save.
At Minnesota, Ricky Bones allowed three runs over seven innings and Yamil Benitez smacked a three-run homer in his Kansas City debut to boost the Royals to a 5-3 win over the Minnesota Twins.
Bones (1-2) scattered seven hits, walked one and struck out five in his second start of the season for Kansas City. Jeff Montgomery worked the ninth for his fourth save.

Benitez homered in the second inning in his first Royals at-bat. "This is my third chance already," said Benitez, who played last year for Montreal. "Two times in the National League and now here in the American League."

In Boston, Jeff Suppan allowed four hits over 7 2/3 innings and Nomar Garciaparra had a double, triple and home run to lead the Boston Red Sox to their seventh victory in nine games, 3-0 over the Oakland Athletics.
Suppan (5-0) walked two and struck out six in combining with Jim Corsi and Heathcliff Slocumb for the shutout.

Boston got on the board in the fifth. Darren Bragg singled and scored on Jeff Frye's double and Garciaparra followed with a triple, plating Frye for a 2-0 lead. Garciaparra hit his second homer in as many days in the eighth to cap the scoring.
